text: This man left home in 1998, and he's only just walking back.
In 1998, Carl Buschby set off from the tip of Chile with $500.
His rule, no cars, planes, or boats to move forward.
And no going home until he walks there.
He crossed the Darien Gap jungle and spent 18 days in a Panama jail.
In 2006, he walked across the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska to Russia.
Then Russia banned him for five years.
Visas stopped him more than mountains did.
Where he couldn't walk, he swam.
288 kilometers across the Caspian Sea, and the English Channel last month.
His first step on British soil since 1998, about 50,000 kilometers, 29 countries.
And today, he's due to walk into his hometown, Hull.
Next time, we take the bus.
This is Boogal. Follow for more geography fun facts.
